subject: TYPEDEF clause
notes: kb/Work PB1303 (wave 1012 J). cite.py --check 13.18.58.4 'The GLOBAL clause applies to the scope of the type-name' OK GR3; --check 8.4.6.2.2 'type-name described with a GLOBAL clause is a global name' OK. A GLOBAL type declaration is now a global name: BinderDriver.BindUnitData hands every container's GLOBAL TYPEDEFs to the contained unit BEFORE data.Bind (DataBinder.InheritGlobalTypeDecls, nearest container first, a local declaration shadowing); DataBinder.TryFindTypeDecl is the ONE type-name lookup (TYPE clause, USAGE POINTER TO type-name, an intrinsic's type-name argument). Golden: the directly contained and the grandchild program use OUTER's T (group with a numeric member and an 88) and the nearer MID's U over OUTER's U; the negative pins that a type-name WITHOUT GLOBAL stays local (COBOL1530). The object-definition clause of 8.4.6.2.2 (a type-name declared in a factory or instance definition is global to its methods) was probed and already conforms.
